thesis.problem: A reconnaissance drone is only useful if the picture it brings back is current, and European armies spent two decades buying small numbers of expensive airframes on procurement cycles measured in years. Ukraine changed the arithmetic: what a unit needs is a system a soldier can carry, launch without a runway, fly beyond line of sight and replace when it is lost, plus a manufacturer close enough to the front to change the software every few weeks as jamming evolves.
thesis.solution: Quantum Systems builds vertical-take-off fixed-wing drones that lift like a helicopter and cruise like an aeroplane, so they need no launcher and still hold an area for hours, and it sells the autonomy stack alongside the airframe. The dual-use framing is deliberate and commercial: the same aircraft surveys pipelines, mines and farmland, which keeps a civilian revenue line under a defence business whose orders arrive in bursts. Its systems flew over 19,000 missions in Ukraine in 2025.

undisclosed.note: This is the round that crossed, and no source has ever printed the number it crossed at. Sifted, Tech.eu, EU-Startups and lead investor Balderton all covered it, and the company's own release, recovered from the Wayback Machine because quantum-systems.com blocks this crawler, gives the round, the investors and the total raised while stating no valuation at all. What is stated flatly rather than as an estimate is the threshold, by Handelsblatt in the same week: “Mit der neuen Finanzierung wird das Start-up mit mehr als einer Milliarde Dollar bewertet.” Under the register's previous rule that sentence could not be recorded, because it contains no numeral to check a figure against, and one of Germany's best-known unicorns was left out on that technicality. The November extension that “tripled its valuation” to above €3 billion is the next figure anyone published, and dividing that by three would be arithmetic rather than a source.
